subject: Hotlane replaystorm causing latency spikes & 5xxs — Strand.ai impact
messages:
From: Maya Rourke <maya@strand.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@strand.ai
Date: 2028-04-01T08:12:34Z
Subject: Urgent: sudden p99 spike + 5xx surge from our tenant (prod)

Hi Soojin —

We’re seeing a sharp increase in end-to-end latency and 5xxs from our production integration with Redwood starting ~08:05 UTC. p50 looks fine but p99 is up from ~320ms to ~1.2s and error rate (5xx) jumped from 0.1% to 4.8%. Throughput observed by our proxy dropped ~30% concurrently.

Attached are a short sample of request IDs and a small slice of the proxy logs (strand_request_samples.log). We’re in the middle of a high-frequency retry loop for a downstream scoring job, but this pattern looks like it’s causing repeated prefix churn on your side and hitting some cache eviction behavior. Can you confirm whether this is being driven by anything on Redwood’s end (KV cache thrash / hotlane blocking)? This is affecting our customers — we need mitigation asap and an ETA for root cause.

We’ve opened an internal incident (INC-5231) and can provide whatever you need.

Thanks,
Maya Rourke
Head of Platform — Strand.ai


From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rourke <maya@strand.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T08:20:05Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden p99 spike + 5xx surge from our tenant (prod)

Thanks for the heads up and the samples, Maya — we’re looking immediately. I’ve paged the inference SREs and the hotlane/KV owners.

Immediate asks:
- Ben: can you confirm whether this matches a KV eviction/repopulation pattern or HOL queueing?
- Maya: can you share whether you rolled any new model or changed request patterns ~08:00 UTC? Any recent retries/bulk replays will change prefix distribution.

We will look at tenant-level prefetch/backfill and hotlane reservation immediately and apply emergency mitigations if needed. I’ll keep you posted every 30m or sooner.

— Soojin
Director, Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T08:36:17Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden p99 spike + 5xx surge from our tenant (prod) — initial triage

Quick triage from the serving plane:
- Observed behavior: multiple tenants show transient KV cache churn, but Strand.ai’s tenant is the top contributor to HOL (head-of-line) blocking on several hotlanes between 08:04–08:14 UTC.
- Evidence: KV eviction rate spiked; prefix miss/repopulate ops increased 12x for the tenant. Several worker queues report long-running prefix-writes that are blocking other requests (classic HOL).
- Root-candidate: a replay pattern — we see an elevated repetition of a handful of prefixes (same prompt family) that cause back-to-back cache populate operations and push other tenant traffic into queue waits.

Emergency mitigations I propose (can be enacted in next 10–15m):
1) Apply a conservative tenant throttle on prefetch/backfill (limit concurrent prefetch to 2) — reduces eviction churn.
2) Temporarily pin a small slot reservation for Strand.ai on hotlane to prevent total starvation of their active sessions (reduces retry amplification).
3) Flip KV policy for the tenant to LRU-lite (aggressive prefix retention for in-flight keys) for 30m window.
4) Blacklist the runaway prefix hash pattern (we can soft-drop prefetch on matching prefix ID) while they roll back their replay.

I’m attaching the internal playbook (playbook_kv_mitigation.md) — it’s a short checklist. I’ll coordinate with ops on rolling these safely.

— Ben
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Maya Rourke <maya@strand.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T08:45:52Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: sudden p99 spike + 5xx surge from our tenant (prod)

Thanks Ben / Soojin — we just confirmed we rolled a canary model and an automated replay job kicked off for a backfill around 08:00 UTC. That explains the repeated prefixes. We’re initiating an immediate rollback of that canary and throttling the replay on our side.

We appreciate the proposed mitigations — please go ahead with whatever is low-risk to reduce customer impact. We’re ready to coordinate an emergency rollback in tandem if you need it.

Apologies for the churn — will update you once our rollback completes (ETA ~15–20m).

— Maya

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rourke <maya@strand.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T09:05:40Z
Subject: Re: Urgent: customer impact & next steps (Strand.ai)

Looping in Laura for account coordination and exec visibility — Strand is on a mid-market enterprise plan and we want to be proactive about credits / SLA conversation if required.

Short-term: prioritize mitigation and keep the customer updated every 15 minutes.
Medium-term (post-stable): schedule a 30-min exec briefing today with Strand engineers, our SREs, and a PM to review guardrails (rate limits, tenant reservations, replay detection).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rourke <maya@strand.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-01T12:45:10Z
Subject: Re: Hotlane replaystorm — mitigation summary and next steps

Update:
- We applied Ben’s mitigations at 08:55 UTC (tenant throttle + temporary slot reservation + KV LRU-lite flip + prefix soft-drop).
- Strand.ai rolled back the canary and throttled the replay at ~08:25–08:30 UTC.
- Observed result: p99 returned to ~340ms and 5xxs dropped to baseline by 09:10 UTC. Throughput recovered to normal by 09:22 UTC.

Immediate follow-ups:
- Postmortem scheduled: 2028-04-02 15:00 UTC (Jira INC-9876).
- Action items: implement tenant replay detection (engine metrics), add automatic prefetch-rate caps per-tenant, refine hotlane reservation defaults, and expose an emergency tenant-mitigation toggle in Console.
- Customer-facing: Marissa to coordinate credits / formal apology; Laura to lead exec briefing.

Attachments included: playbook_kv_mitigation.md (runbook), tenant_logs.zip (redacted logs for the 08:00–09:30 window).

Thanks everyone — I’ll post the postmortem link in this thread after the RCA.

— Soojin
Director, Reliability — Redwood Inference
